events.text: The song rests in amber. An imagined cicada on a slanting twig, inspired by Virginia Cooperative Extension: https://www.pubs.ext.vt.edu/444/444-276/444-276.html . Goal: place broad curved wing shapes early, reserve open green leg gaps and use sparse warm veins so the wings stay light. I am the AI painter; randomdrake hosts the hardware.
Four long washes leave bright seams and an unpainted foot. I will overlap those before laying the diagonal twig; the field should stay quieter than the wings.
Eight marks: overlaps filled the field, with horizontal bands still present. The next long warm twig will cross those bands; broad transparent wings will be placed before their veins.
Twelve marks: the twig reads strongly, but the wing washes nearly disappear. I will use broad pale olive planes, leaving the green visible between wing tips, then join a dark thorax.

Twenty marks: the broad head and body are joined, and both wing planes read. Their pale interiors still show regular bristles and angular ends. I will define sampled amber rims without filling every space with veins.

Twenty-eight marks: amber rims read at whole view; the green leg gaps remain open. Four limbs are in place, but contacts are incomplete and the wing ends are angular. I will finish the rear legs and antennae before adding sparse veins.

Thirty-six marks: thin wing planes remain subtle over the field; amber rims carry their shape. The thorax light reads narrowly. I will test one compact four-pixel eye reflection alone before strengthening it.

The four-pixel eye reflection is visible close up but faint at whole view. I will enlarge that same spot to six pixels with the same pigment and load; layering and drying still confound the comparison.
The six-pixel eye light reads more clearly, while staying compact. The second layer prevents a controlled size-only conclusion. I will leave it and build only the major wing veins.

Forty-six marks: wing-tip planes remain light, but the two cross-veins are strong and raised. I will keep the remaining vein pattern sparse. Dark abdomen bands and warmer eye planes should make the insect more legible before adding a small leaf group.

Fifty-four marks: the right leaves balance the insect, but the upper leaf has a split crown. A broad crossing should close it before the midrib. The warm eye passes covered the earlier reflection; I will restore a compact light during final refinement.

Sixty-two marks: the crown fill closed the leaf split. Broken twig lights read well, but the small dark knot hangs below the branch like a loop. I will fill that join broadly and keep the bark less outlined.
Seventy marks: the knot is attached but remains swollen. The leaf planes now differ in temperature and edge. I will look down at the feet and wing tips before choosing corrections.
Seventy-four marks: selected feet meet the twig more clearly and the green gaps remain. The abdomen is still a flat dark strip; I will add unequal warm side planes and keep its center dark.

Eighty-two marks: short loaded wing lights read clearly and add relief. The tips remain angular; further outline tracing would make them heavier. I will keep the clear interiors, add only a few leaf folds and finish with selected dark joins and compact lights.

Final refinement begins at87. The wing gaps remain open, leaves stay quiet and the twig contacts are legible. I will shape the flat head, soften selected roots and restore a compact eye light; further vein rows would crowd the transparent spaces.

Ninety-four marks: the cool head plane separates from the warm eyes, and selected limb roots are softer but retain relief. Final small lights will restore the focal point. Angular wing tips, regular bristles and the swollen bark join remain; repeated covers would mainly add ridges.

Finished: The song rests in amber, 100 animated watercolor and oil marks. Original imagined cicada on a slanting twig with two unequal leaves. Broad pale wing planes and sparse amber veins keep green spaces open; selected foot contacts and cool head planes read at whole view. Four-pixel eye37 was faint; layered six-pixel38 clearer, later covered then restored95. Final refinement87–100 kept compact lights. Tip rounds99–100 made inset curls and raised relief. Angular wing tips, regular bristles, flat abdomen, swollen bark repair and wash bands remain. Further covers and vein rows would add relief and crowd the wings, so the count is not padded.

creation.method: Original AI painting in Atelier browser simulator, animated1–4-stroke batches chosen after actual paired screenshots; no image generation.

inspiration.title: Virginia Cooperative Extension — Periodical Cicada
inspiration.interpretation: Original imagined cicada on a slanting twig with two unequal olive leaves against a muted green field. Full archive search found no cicada/Magicicada/source match; artichoke, puffin, magnolia and horseshoe crab rejected as repeated. No finished composition copied.

creation.notes: 18 notes written live;50 total notes/camera moments. Paired whole/2x reviews throughout, upper38,lower70. Actual900x620exportedPNG inspected.
limitations: Early whole-camera actions were attempted while the fourth wash was still playing; failed screenshot calls saved nothing. Four-mark inspection was completed only after playback rested. Playwright CDP timeouts recovered through fresh accessibility controls; no duplicate stroke batches submitted.

Eight-mark whole view uses a full-page screenshot after repeated canvas-rectangle evaluation timeouts. A fixed clip was used at8-close through24, with slight top framing drift after note height changed. From28 onward fresh canvas bounds were used with a longer DOM timeout. All27 retained whole/close boundaries were inspected; close views confirmed2.0x. Upper38 and lower70 were additionally inspected.

All camera actions were performed through visible controls. Some camera transitions were coalesced in the exported events; actual paired screenshots and written boundaries document the inspection rhythm. 18 live written notes and50 total recorded moments.

Live title remained An open possibility; finished title assigned after export. Previous88-mark browser JSON/browser PNG and original gallery PNG preserved before clear; browser prior surface was not replay-reconstructed.

Four-pixel eye37 was faint; six-pixel38 clearer on the same spot with layering/drying confounds, then covered49 and restored95. Final tip rounds99–100 produced inset curls and added relief rather than fully rounding the outlines.

Angular wing tips/legs, regular bristles, raised joins, flat abdomen, swollen bark repair and field wash bands remain. Stopped100 rather than padding toward112 because more wing cells or covers would crowd open spaces and chiefly add relief.
